title: Work, energy, and power
summary: Learn about work, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, and power.
cards.0.h: Work: when a force moves something
cards.0.p: When a force moves an object, work is done. Work is W = F·d·cosθ, where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. Its unit is the joule, and 1 J = 1 N·m.
cards.0.key: If a 50 N force acts at a 60° angle over 4 m, then W = 50·4·0.5 = 100 J (cos60° = 0.5).
cards.1.p: If the force helps the motion, the work is positive. If it opposes the motion (friction), the work is negative. If the force is perpendicular to the motion or the object does not move, the work is zero.
cards.1.key: cos0° = 1, cos90° = 0, and cos180° = −1. Even if pushing a wall tires you out, you do no work in the physics sense.
cards.2.p: A moving object has kinetic energy, given by KE = ½·m·v². The speed enters this formula squared. So when the speed doubles, the energy becomes 4 times larger.
cards.2.key: A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s has a kinetic energy of ½·1000·20² = 200 000 J.
cards.3.p: An object lifted higher gains potential energy, given by PE = m·g·h. h is measured from the zero level you choose. A 2 kg book on a 1.5 m shelf has a potential energy of 29.4 J.
cards.3.key: 2·9.8·1.5 = 29.4 J. Here g = 9.8 m/s² was used, but problems often take g = 10.
cards.3.once.soru: If you put the same book twice as high, what happens to its potential energy?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: PE = m·g·h. When h doubles, PE doubles too.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: The square appears only with speed, in kinetic energy. Potential energy is directly proportional to height.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: PE increases as the height increases.
cards.4.p: The net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy (Wnet = ΔKE). A cart at rest pushed with a 10 N force over 5 m gains 50 J of kinetic energy.
cards.4.key: The net work is the final kinetic energy minus the initial kinetic energy. With 50 J of energy, a 2 kg cart reaches about 7.1 m/s.
cards.4.once.soru: A net work of 200 J is done on a car at rest. What is its kinetic energy, in J?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: The net work equals the change in kinetic energy, and 0 + 200 = 200 J.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Because net work is done, the car speeds up.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: All of the net work goes into kinetic energy.
cards.5.p: As you just saw with the ball, while the potential energy decreases, the kinetic energy increases by the same amount. The sum of KE and PE is called mechanical energy. If only gravity does work, this sum stays constant.
cards.5.key: KE + PE = constant (if only gravity does work). If work is done from outside (a push), the mechanical energy changes.
cards.5.etk.soru: Drop the ball from different heights. Does the mass change the impact speed? (No air resistance.)
cards.6.p: With friction, part of the mechanical energy turns into heat. A child going down a slide slows down, and the slide warms up. The energy turned into heat equals the work done by friction, and the total energy is conserved.
cards.6.key: The work done by friction is the initial energy minus the final energy. For a skater who starts with 100 J and ends with 70 J, friction did 30 J of work.
cards.7.h: The F–x graph and spring energy
cards.7.p: The area under a force–extension graph gives the work. For a spring F = k·x, so the graph is a triangle. The area of this triangle is the energy stored in the spring, PE = ½·k·x².
cards.7.key: If k = 200 N/m and x = 0.1 m, the stored energy is ½·200·0.01 = 1 J.
cards.8.p: In machines, part of the energy turns into unwanted heat. Efficiency is the useful energy divided by the energy supplied, times 100. Efficiency never exceeds 100%.
cards.8.once.soru: A bulb turns 20 J of every 100 J of electrical energy into light. What is its efficiency, in percent?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: The ratio of useful energy to supplied energy is 20 / 100 = 0.2, which is 20%.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: 80% is the part that goes into heat, not the useful part.
cards.9.h: Power: how fast work is done
cards.9.p: Power is the work done per unit time, P = W / t. Its unit is the watt, and 1 W = 1 J/s. A person who runs up the stairs uses more power than one who walks up.
cards.9.key: A 50 kg person who climbs 3 m does about 1470 J of work. Doing it in 5 s takes 294 W, and in 10 s it takes 147 W. 1 kWh is 3.6 million J.
cards.10.p: If an object moves at a constant speed v under a force F, the power is P = F·v. If you push a crate with a 500 N force at a constant 2 m/s, the power is 1000 W.
cards.10.key: P = W/t = F·d/t = F·v. That is why you shift to a low gear on a hill. It gives you a large force at a low speed.
cards.10.svg#5: net force zero, yet the push does 1000 J each second
cards.10.once.soru: A car with constant engine power starts up a hill and needs a larger force. What happens to its speed?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: If P = F·v is constant, v gets smaller when F gets larger.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: With constant power, the speed cannot increase when the force increases.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The product F·v is constant. So when F changes, v changes too.
cards.11.p: Energy comes in many forms. Kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical, light, sound, and nuclear energy are some of them. All are measured in joules and can turn into one another. The total energy is conserved.
cards.11.svg#8: Energy changes form; the total is conserved
cards.11.key: At a dam, potential energy first turns into kinetic energy (turbine), then into electrical energy (generator), and finally into light and heat (lamp).
cards.11.once.soru: In what order does the water's energy change at a dam?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: The water falls from a height and speeds up, it turns the turbine, and the generator produces electricity.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: That is a thermal power plant. No fuel burns at a dam.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: That is a nuclear power plant.
cards.12.p:
Work is W = F·d·cosθ, and its unit is the joule.
KE = ½mv² and PE = mgh. The net work equals the change in kinetic energy.
If only gravity does work, KE + PE stays constant. Friction turns energy into heat.
Power is P = W/t = F·v.
For a spring PE = ½kx². Efficiency is the ratio of useful energy to supplied energy.
quiz.0.q: A 2 kg box is released from rest at the top of a 5 m high ramp and reaches the bottom at 8 m/s. How many joules did friction turn into heat? (g = 10 m/s²)
quiz.0.e: The initial energy is m·g·h = 2·10·5 = 100 J, and the final energy is ½·2·8² = 64 J. Friction turned 100 − 64 = 36 J into heat.
quiz.1.q: You apply the force. Are you doing work in the physics sense?
quiz.1.ogeler.0.0: Lifting a book onto a shelf
quiz.1.ogeler.4.0: Holding a weight in the air
quiz.1.e: For work to be done, there must be a displacement along the direction of the force. The book, the box, and the ball move in the direction of the force. The wall and the weight held in the air do not move. Even if you get tired, W = 0 in these cases.
quiz.2.q: A net force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg object at rest over 10 m. What is the object's final speed, in m/s?
quiz.2.e: The net work is 20·10 = 200 J, and it equals the change in kinetic energy. Since ½·4·v² = 200, v² = 100 and v = 10 m/s.
quiz.3.q: A motor uses 600 J of energy in 3 s and does 450 J of useful work. What are its efficiency and useful power?
quiz.3.e: The efficiency is 450 / 600 = 75%. The useful power is 450 J / 3 s = 150 W. 200 W is the power supplied.
quiz.3.y.1: If you got 200 W, you divided the supplied 600 J by 3 s. The useful power is 450 J / 3 s.
quiz.3.y.2: Efficiency is the ratio of useful work to supplied energy, which is 450/600. Efficiency cannot exceed 100%.
quiz.3.y.3: 25% is the part that is lost. Efficiency is the share of useful work, 450/600 = 75%.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Change the angle of the rope, drop the ball, and run up the stairs.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Work is the part of the force along the motion times the distance. You pull a box 5 m with a force of 40 N. Set the angle of the rope and make the work 100 J.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: W = 40 · 5 · cos60° = 200 · 0.5 = 100 J. As the angle grows, the share of the force along the motion shrinks, and at 90° it is zero.
A:adimlar.1.metin: You walk along a level road at constant speed, holding a heavy bag. Your arm holds the bag upward, while the bag moves horizontally. So θ = 90°.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: How much work does your arm do on the bag?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Getting tired does not mean doing physical work. What is cos90°?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: For negative work, the force must oppose the motion, as friction does. Here the force is perpendicular to the motion.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: cos90° = 0. Your tiredness comes from the energy used inside your muscles, not from work transferred to the bag.
A:adimlar.2.metin: A 1000 kg car moves at 10 m/s, and its kinetic energy is 50 000 J. Set the speed and make the kinetic energy 9 times larger.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: At 30 m/s the kinetic energy is ½ · 1000 · 30² = 450 000 J. The speed went up 3 times, and the energy went up 3² = 9 times. That is why a fast vehicle is so much harder to stop.
A:adimlar.3.metin: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 5 m, and its potential energy is 2 · 9.8 · 5 = 98 J. Only gravity does work on it.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What is the ball's kinetic energy, in J, as it touches the ground?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The ball is fastest as it touches the ground, so its kinetic energy is largest there.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: That is the value halfway down.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: At the ground the potential energy is zero, and all of the lost 98 J has become kinetic energy. Since ½ · 2 · v² = 98 J, the ball hits the ground at about 9.9 m/s.
A:adimlar.4.metin: You release a skater from the edge of the ramp (g = 10 m/s²). Change the height, the mass, and the friction. The bar below shows how the energy changes form. Find out the following for yourself.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.0.yazi: On the frictionless ramp, find the height that makes the speed at the bottom 10 m/s.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.0.tamam: Since m·g·h = ½·m·v², v = √(2gh) = √(2·10·5) = 10 m/s. The skater rises to 5 m again on the other side, because KE + PE always stays the same.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.1.yazi: At 5 m, set the mass to 40 and then to 80 kg. Does the speed at the bottom change?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.1.tamam: The speed did not change (10 m/s), because m appears on both sides and cancels. But the energy doubled, from 2000 J to 4000 J.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.2.yazi: Turn friction on and watch until the skater stops. Where did the energy go?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.2.tamam: The mechanical energy (KE + PE) decreased, but the length of the bar did not change. The missing part turned into heat. Energy is never destroyed; it only changes form.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Power is work divided by time. On the same stairs, a 50 kg person climbs 3 m and does about 1470 J of work. Set the climbing time and make the power 210 W.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: 1470 / 7 = 210 W. If the same work is done in less time, the power goes up. The 1 kWh on an electricity bill is 3.6 million J.
A:adimlar.6.baslik: The spring and the F–x graph
A:adimlar.6.metin: The spring constant is k = 200 N/m, and the energy stored in the spring is ½·k·x². Stretch the spring and store 4 J of energy in it.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: At x = 0.2 m the force is F = 200 · 0.2 = 40 N, and the area of the triangle is ½ · 0.2 · 40 = 4 J. The extension doubled (from 10 cm to 20 cm), while the energy became 4 times larger (from 1 J to 4 J).
A:kapanis.0: Work is W = F·d·cosθ, and its unit is the joule. If the force is perpendicular to the motion or the object does not move, the work is zero.
A:kapanis.1: Kinetic energy is KE = ½·m·v², and when the speed doubles the energy becomes 4 times larger. Potential energy is PE = m·g·h.
A:kapanis.2: If only gravity does work, KE + PE stays constant. Friction turns part of the mechanical energy into heat, but the total energy is still conserved.
A:kapanis.3: Power is P = W / t, and its unit is the watt. If the same work is done in less time, the power goes up.
A:kapanis.4: The area under a force–extension graph gives the work. The energy stored in a spring is ½·k·x².
